summary: Read an unordered list of integers. Negatives, zeros, and repeated values may all appear. Starting at 1 and counting upward through the positive integers, find the smallest one that never occurs in the list, and write it. Base the decision only on the values actually read, without assuming a fixed ceiling printed beside the task. When 1 itself is absent, the answer is 1.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is tokens in the same order as the method parameters.
